recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the applied FHIR-28235 wording on the authoritative Communication narrative page without broadening the unresolved Communication-vs-messaging policy question.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request asking to clarify confusing Communication wording, especially the old statement that Communication could be a record even if planned or failed and whether Communication can represent an actual communication flow.
initial_application: Commit 40aa5c88300a803dc5d821194e74821ab60e2340 applied FHIR-28235 with FHIR-40214 by updating the Communication Boundaries and Relationships paragraph, but the old planned-or-failed Scope sentence remained in the same built narrative source.
additional_context: FHIR-40214 and duplicate issues FHIR-30393/FHIR-34111 support actual-flow use cases such as secure messaging; FHIR-40760 touched the same paragraph and has already been reconciled on the combined branch. The reporter's Zulip thread shows the concern came from clinical-email-style Communication content, while unresolved FHIR-23061 remains broader background on Communication vs messaging boundaries.
reconciliation: Changed source/communication/communication-introduction.xml so Scope and Usage now says Communication is a record of a communication that has occurred or where the communication process has at least initiated, removing the stale suggestion that merely planned communications are in scope.
source_changes: source/communication/communication-introduction.xml: Replaced the Scope and Usage sentence "even if it is planned or has failed" with the final FHIR-28235 process-initiated wording.
